Supply against demand around each place: the two-step floating catchment area

Source: R/location.R
floating_catchment.Rd

Step 1: the supply of each facility (places, staff, beds) is divided by the demand within its catchment. Step 2: each demand point adds up the ratios of the facilities within its catchment. The result, per demand point, is supply per unit of demand, which accounts both for how near the facilities are and for how many others compete for them (Luo and Wang, 2003).

Usage

floating_catchment(
  network,
  demand,
  supply,
  cutoff = NULL,
  decay_function = "step",
  decay_value = NULL,
  demand_colname = NULL,
  supply_colname = NULL,
  mode = "WALK",
  mode_egress = "WALK",
  departure_datetime = NULL,
  percentile = 50L,
  max_trip_duration = NULL,
  travel_times = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

network

The network of build_network(); may be NULL with travel_times.

demand

The demand points: a data.frame with id, lon and lat, or a POINT sf with an id column, and, with demand_colname, their weights.

supply

The facilities: a data.frame or POINT sf with id, lon, lat and, with supply_colname, their capacities.

cutoff

The catchment in minutes; NULL with "fixed_exponential".

decay_function

A string: "step", "exponential", "fixed_exponential", "linear" or "logistic" (see accessibility()).

decay_value

The parameter of "fixed_exponential", "linear" and "logistic", as in accessibility(); NULL for the others.

demand_colname, supply_colname

The names of the numeric columns with the weight of each demand point and the capacity of each facility; NULL for 1 each.

mode

A character vector, the transport modes (see the section "Transport modes"). Defaults to "WALK".

mode_egress

A string, the mode from the last stop to the destination: "WALK" (the default), "BICYCLE" or "CAR". Ignored without public transport.

departure_datetime

A POSIXct, the departure date and time (see the section "Date and time"). Required with public transport.

percentile

The travel-time percentile used (public transport over a time window), a whole number from 1 to 99.

max_trip_duration

The longest trip considered, in minutes. NULL: cutoff (rounded up) for "step", 120 for the other functions.

travel_times

A table of travel times to use instead of routing: from_id (demand point), to_id (site) and travel_time_pXX for the percentile (or travel_time), in minutes, as travel_time_matrix() returns it. A pair that is absent or has a missing time is unreachable; rows of other points are ignored. With it, network and the routing arguments are not used and the points need only their id.

...

Any other argument of travel_time_matrix(), by its full name: time_window, walk_speed, max_walk_time, seed and so on (not percentiles or output_dir).

Value

A list of two tables:

  • demand: one row per demand point: id (with lon and lat when given), demand (its weight) and accessibility (supply per unit of demand).

  • supply: one row per facility: id, supply, catchment_demand (the weighted demand in its catchment) and ratio (supply divided by that demand; 0 when the catchment holds no demand).

    Tables are tibbles by default; options(peabiru.output = "data.frame") gives base data.frames and options(peabiru.output = "data.table") gives data.tables (see peabiru-package).

Details

With decay_function = "step" a pair of demand point and facility counts in full up to cutoff minutes (travel time <= cutoff) and not at all beyond: the two-step floating catchment area in its original form. Any other decay function gives the enhanced form, in which nearer pairs weigh more, in both steps (Luo and Qi, 2009, with a continuous weight in place of their travel-time zones); the functions and their values are those of accessibility(), and the trips beyond the cutoff still count with their weight, up to max_trip_duration.

The sum over the demand points of demand times accessibility equals the supply of the facilities that have any demand in their catchment. The travel times are computed with travel_time_matrix(), from each demand point to each facility, or taken from travel_times.

References

Luo W, Wang F (2003). "Measures of spatial accessibility to health care in a GIS environment: synthesis and a case study in the Chicago region." Environment and Planning B: Planning and Design, 30(6), 865-884. doi:10.1068/b29120 .

Luo W, Qi Y (2009). "An enhanced two-step floating catchment area (E2SFCA) method for measuring spatial accessibility to primary care physicians." Health & Place, 15(4), 1100-1107. doi:10.1016/j.healthplace.2009.06.002 .

See also

locate_facilities() to choose where to open facilities.

Other location functions: locate_facilities()

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo", package = "peabiru")
network <- build_network(data_path, n_threads = 2)
points <- read.csv(file.path(data_path, "spo_points.csv"))

# schools per resident within a 20-minute walk
schools <- points[points$schools > 0, ]
fca <- floating_catchment(
  network, points, schools, cutoff = 20,
  demand_colname = "population", supply_colname = "schools",
  mode = "WALK", n_threads = 2
)
head(fca$demand)
